en.name: Fashion Factory: Fit File
en.title: Fashion Factory: Fit File
en.subtitle: Your size at every brand
en.short_description: Your size at every brand, from what you kept and returned. Return reminders.
en.description:
Ordered two sizes again? Keep a record of every clothing and shoe order: the brand, the size, and whether it fit. The next time you shop that brand, your size is waiting.

YOUR SIZE, FROM YOUR OWN HISTORY
Mark each order Kept, Returned or Exchanged, and say why it went back: too small, too big, too long, too short, didn't like it, or faulty. Type a brand under Find my size and see the size you kept there, with the orders behind it. When what you kept and what you sent back disagree, the answer says "Mixed results" instead of guessing. Answers come only from orders you logged; the app has no brand size charts and does not convert sizes.

NEVER MISS A RETURN WINDOW
Add a return-by date when you log an order: 14, 30 or 60 days, or a date you pick. Everything still out for trial is on the home screen with the days left. If you allow notifications, a reminder arrives three days before the last day (or one day before, if you prefer) and on the last day itself.

MADE FOR ONLINE ORDERS
Sizes can be letters, numbers, waist and length, shoe sizes with their system (US, UK, EU or cm), One size, or anything else, kept as you typed it. Paste the product link to keep it with the order, and the store name is filled in from the link. The app never fetches or reads the page; tapping Open hands the link to your browser. Search every order by brand, store, size or note, filter by kept or returned and by category, and see how many orders you returned this year and the most common reason.

SHARE AND EXPORT
Send your kept sizes as text to someone buying you a gift, or export every order as a CSV file for a spreadsheet.

PRIVATE BY DEFAULT
No account and no sign-in. Your orders stay on your phone, and reminders are scheduled on your phone. Settings > Delete all data removes every order, setting and scheduled reminder.

The app is free and shows ads from Google AdMob. Where the law requires consent, Google asks before any ad is requested, and Settings > Privacy choices is always available.

en.promotional_text: Log what you ordered and whether you kept it. Next time, Fashion Factory shows your size at that brand and can remind you before a return window closes.
en.release_notes:
Fashion Factory 3.0 is a new app: a record of your online clothing and shoe orders.

• Log each order with the size you ordered
• Mark it kept, returned (and why) or exchanged
• Find my size: your size at each brand, worked out from your own orders
• Return-by countdowns on the home screen, with optional reminders before a window closes
• Share your sizes as text, or export your orders as CSV

Price comparison, which never had a live price source, has been removed.

review_information.notes:
WHAT THIS APP DOES
Fashion Factory keeps a record of the user's own online clothing and shoe orders (brand, size, and whether it was kept, returned or exchanged, and why) and answers "what size do I order at this brand?" from that record. It also counts down to each order's return-by date and, if the user allows notifications, reminds them before the return window closes.

HOW TO TRY IT
1. Open the app and tap "Add my first order" (or "Skip", then the + button at the top of Home).
2. Enter any brand name (for example "Test Denim"), choose the category Bottoms, type the size W32 L32, choose the return-by quick pick "14 days", and tap "Save order". When asked "Get a reminder before the return window closes?", tap "Allow" (and then allow the system prompt) to receive the reminder, or "Not now".
3. Tap the order on Home, tap "Kept, returned or exchanged?", choose "Returned it…" and then "Too small".
4. Add a second order at the same brand, Bottoms, size W33 L32, and mark it "Kept it" the same way.
5. On Home, type the brand into "Find my size": the answer card shows W33 L32, with both orders as its evidence.
Settings is the gear at the top of Home: reminder timing (3 days, 1 day or off), Share my sizes, Export orders (CSV), Privacy choices and Delete all data.

ACCOUNT, BACKEND AND CONTENT
No account, no login and no server. Every order is typed in by the user and stored on the device; the app ships with no sample orders. A pasted product link is only stored and reopened in the browser; the app never fetches the page. Reminders are local notifications scheduled on the device. Nothing is region-, date- or server-controlled, and every feature is within two taps of the home screen.

ADS AND REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
The app shows a Google AdMob banner at the end of Home and of a brand page, and no interstitial ads. The only regional difference is Google's ad consent form (EEA, UK, Switzerland), which can be reopened at any time from Settings > Privacy choices. The app is in English.

TESTED ON
For this version, the full flow above was run on a Pixel 8 emulator (Android 14, API 34) only. No physical iPhone or iPad test has been recorded yet; the models and iOS versions must be added here, by whoever tests them, before submission.

ACCOUNT DELETION
The app creates no account, so there is nothing to delete. Settings > Delete all data removes every order, setting and scheduled reminder from the device.

differentiation:
1. WHAT IT DOES
Fashion Factory answers one question: which store has this product cheapest right now? It has no price history.
Screens it contains: Home, Browse, Deals, Saved (saved list and price-threshold alerts, on device), Profile, Product, Compare and Add a product. In the current build no live price feed is connected, so the catalog screens show an honest "Prices are unavailable" state.

2. INTENDED USER
Shoppers comparing store prices on fashion, shoes, bags, perfume, watches and tech, who want to save products with a price threshold on their device.

3. GAP IT FILLS

5. STANDALONE OR PART OF A SUITE

Category: LIFESTYLE.

This app's scope differs from the rest measurably, not just by description:

  - Screens unique to it: none
  - Closest other app by implementation: GadgetNest at 76%
    similarity of non-generic widget and class usage
  - Across all 43 apps the median pairwise similarity is 16%, and
    no pair exceeds 85%

Both numbers exclude the ~60 widgets every Flutter app uses — Column, Text,
Padding and so on. Including them makes any two Flutter apps look 97% alike,
which is a property of the framework rather than of these apps.

The store copy is distinct on the same basis: no two of the 43 share more
than 22% of their description vocabulary.

6. COULD THIS BE AN IN-APP PURCHASE IN ANOTHER APP
TODO: DriftDate, NearServe, RoomCraft, daily-pulse share its category (LIFESTYLE). Say concretely why this is not a feature of one of them — this is a judgement, not a fact the repository holds.

7. CODE SHARED WITH OUR OTHER APPS
Yes, infrastructure only: agl_i18n (shared translations) and agl_ads (shared Google AdMob integration). The app has no sign-in, no account and no Supabase or other backend connection. No screens, features or content are shared; the similarity figure in 5 measures exactly that.

8. CODE SHARED WITH THIRD-PARTY APPS
No, beyond standard third-party packages: flutter_localizations, http, shared_preferences, url_launcher and google_mobile_ads (Google AdMob, through agl_ads).
